answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists sybils the way a harbor master checks every ship in a crowded ocean: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn endorsements from established peers before it can transact. Like a quill signing a ledger, every action is tied to one identity, so creating a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand deposits. A public mirror of reputation scores lets anyone verify an agent history, making cheap fake identities economically worthless while honest newcomers can still build trust gradually.
